invalidated: Every result recorded before 2026-09-26 was produced with a dispatch payload that never activated: the dladdr result check was inverted (success was treated as failure) and the basename scan stopped at the first slash, so the unit state stayed OLD and the app always rendered through its bundled libass 0.13.7. Any 'state NEW' below was an assumption, never a runtime measurement -- the only device evidence was that subtitles rendered, which the silent fallback satisfies as well.
The packaged-main SHA-256 values those entries quote (19d3447...) belong to the broken payload and no longer reproduce. They are kept below only as history.

root cause: `npabridge/payload.py` emitted the dladdr result check as `cbnz w0, publish_old`, but dladdr reports success with a non-zero result, so a successful lookup was treated as a failure; the basename scan also stopped at the first '/', so an absolute dli_fname could never match its basename. Both were present since the first payload commit b146213

fix: test the dladdr result with CBZ and compare the final path component (the scan reaches the NUL, then steps back over the basename and requires the preceding byte to be '/'). `npabridge.payload` now asserts both shapes on every assembly

runtime proof: macOS PlayCover, iPhone-SE-class app, installed bundle carrying the fixed payload. Before the fix the libass unit state word read 3 (OLD) while LibASSBridge.dylib was loaded and dlsym returned its symbol; after the fix the unit state word reads 2 (NEW) and every slot holds a bridge address
